Question: The abdominal muscles can be trained by doing a sit up and a crunch with stretched legs. In which of these exercises will a muscle other than the m. rectus abdominis play an important role?
B: Crunch: internal obliquus and external abdominus m.
Explanation (EN): In a full sit-up the trunk flexes at the hip, so the hip flexors (m. iliopsoas) do much of the work. A crunch only curls the spine and isolates the rectus abdominis more.
Explicación (ES): En un sit-up completo el tronco se flexiona en la cadera, por lo que los flexores de cadera (m. iliopsoas) hacen gran parte del trabajo. Un crunch solo enrolla la columna y aísla más el recto abdominal.

Question: What is NOT a movement pattern (plane) of the human body?
Explanation (EN): The three anatomical planes are sagittal, frontal and transverse. 'Diagonal plane' is not one of them.
Explicación (ES): Los tres planos anatómicos son sagital, frontal y transversal. El 'plano diagonal' no es uno de ellos.

Question: By flexion we mean...
Explanation (EN): Flexion is bending a joint, which decreases the angle between the bones. Stretching (straightening) a joint is extension.
Explicación (ES): La flexión es doblar una articulación, lo que reduce el ángulo entre los huesos. Estirar una articulación es la extensión.

Question: A function of the skeleton is?
Explanation (EN): The skeleton gives the body its shape and support, protects organs, enables movement (as levers), stores minerals and produces blood cells.
Explicación (ES): El esqueleto da forma y soporte al cuerpo, protege los órganos, permite el movimiento (como palancas), almacena minerales y produce células sanguíneas.

Question: Skeletal muscle comprises approximately .. % of the total body mass in normal adults.
Explanation (EN): Skeletal muscle makes up roughly 40% of total body mass in a healthy adult.
Explicación (ES): El músculo esquelético constituye aproximadamente el 40% de la masa corporal total en un adulto sano.

Question: What kind of joint is the elbow joint?
Explanation (EN): The elbow (humero-ulnar joint) is a hinge joint: it allows flexion and extension in one plane.
Explicación (ES): El codo (articulación húmero-cubital) es una articulación en bisagra: permite flexión y extensión en un solo plano.

Question: How are muscles built from large to small?
B: Muscle bundles, muscle fibres, myofibrils, sarcomeres
C: Myofibrils, sarcomeres, muscle fibres, muscle bundles
D: Muscle bundles, muscle fibres, sarcomeres, myofibrils
Explanation (EN): Muscle → muscle bundles (fascicles) → muscle fibres (cells) → myofibrils → sarcomeres, the smallest contractile unit.
Explicación (ES): Músculo → haces musculares (fascículos) → fibras musculares (células) → miofibrillas → sarcómeros, la unidad contráctil más pequeña.

Question: Bones are grouped into four main categories:
A: Long bones, short bones, flat bones and irregular bones
B: Long bones, short bones, thin bones, thick bones
Explanation (EN): Bones are classified by shape: long (femur), short (carpals), flat (sternum, skull) and irregular (vertebrae).
Explicación (ES): Los huesos se clasifican por su forma: largos (fémur), cortos (carpos), planos (esternón, cráneo) e irregulares (vértebras).

Question: Muscle consists of three types of muscle tissue:
A: Skeletal muscle tissue, cardiac muscle tissue and strength muscle tissue
B: Skeletal muscle tissue, cardiac muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue
C: Skeletal muscle tissue, cardio muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue
D: Energy muscle tissue, cardiac muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue
Explanation (EN): The three types are skeletal (voluntary, striated), cardiac (heart) and smooth (organs, blood vessels). Watch the wording: 'cardiac', not 'cardio'.
Explicación (ES): Los tres tipos son esquelético (voluntario, estriado), cardíaco (corazón) y liso (órganos, vasos sanguíneos). Ojo con la palabra: 'cardíaco', no 'cardio'.

Question: What is NOT a role of the skeletal muscle?
A: To hold or move the body and its segments
D: To move blood around the body
Explanation (EN): Moving blood around the body is the job of the heart (cardiac muscle). Skeletal muscle moves and holds the body, maintains posture and produces heat.
Explicación (ES): Mover la sangre por el cuerpo es la función del corazón (músculo cardíaco). El músculo esquelético mueve y sostiene el cuerpo, mantiene la postura y produce calor.

Question: What is the smallest contractile unit of a muscle?
Explanation (EN): The sarcomere, made of actin and myosin filaments, is the smallest functional unit that contracts.
Explicación (ES): El sarcómero, formado por filamentos de actina y miosina, es la unidad funcional más pequeña que se contrae.

Question: Which two protein filaments slide over each other during a muscle contraction?
Explanation (EN): According to the sliding filament theory, myosin heads pull the actin filaments toward the centre of the sarcomere.
Explicación (ES): Según la teoría de los filamentos deslizantes, las cabezas de miosina tiran de los filamentos de actina hacia el centro del sarcómero.

Question: By extension we mean...
D: Moving a limb away from the midline
Explanation (EN): Extension straightens a joint and increases the angle between the bones; it is the opposite of flexion.
Explicación (ES): La extensión endereza una articulación y aumenta el ángulo entre los huesos; es lo contrario de la flexión.

Question: Moving a limb away from the midline of the body is called...
Explanation (EN): Abduction moves away from the midline (e.g. lateral raise). Adduction 'adds' the limb back to the body.
Explicación (ES): La abducción aleja el miembro de la línea media (p. ej., elevación lateral). La aducción lo acerca de nuevo al cuerpo.

Question: In which plane does a lateral raise take place?
Explanation (EN): Sideways movements (abduction/adduction) happen in the frontal plane, which divides the body into front and back.
Explicación (ES): Los movimientos laterales (abducción/aducción) ocurren en el plano frontal, que divide el cuerpo en parte anterior y posterior.

Question: In which plane does a squat or a biceps curl mainly take place?
Explanation (EN): Forward and backward movements (flexion/extension) take place in the sagittal plane, which divides the body into left and right.
Explicación (ES): Los movimientos hacia delante y atrás (flexión/extensión) ocurren en el plano sagital, que divide el cuerpo en izquierda y derecha.

Question: A trunk rotation (e.g. a wood chop or Russian twist) takes place mainly in the...
Explanation (EN): Rotations take place in the transverse (horizontal) plane, which divides the body into upper and lower halves.
Explicación (ES): Las rotaciones ocurren en el plano transversal (horizontal), que divide el cuerpo en mitad superior e inferior.

Question: What type of joint is the shoulder joint?
Explanation (EN): The shoulder (glenohumeral) joint is a ball-and-socket joint and allows movement in all three planes.
Explicación (ES): El hombro (articulación glenohumeral) es una articulación esférica (enartrosis) y permite movimiento en los tres planos.

Question: Which joint is a saddle joint?
Explanation (EN): The carpometacarpal joint of the thumb is the classic saddle joint, which lets the thumb oppose the fingers.
Explicación (ES): La articulación carpometacarpiana del pulgar es la articulación en silla de montar típica; permite oponer el pulgar a los dedos.

Question: The joint between the first and second cervical vertebrae (atlas and axis), which lets you shake your head 'no', is a...
Explanation (EN): The atlanto-axial joint is a pivot joint and allows rotation only.
Explicación (ES): La articulación atlantoaxial es una articulación en pivote y solo permite rotación.

Question: Which muscle is the agonist during a biceps curl?
Explanation (EN): The agonist (prime mover) produces the movement: the biceps brachii flexes the elbow. The triceps is the antagonist.
Explicación (ES): El agonista (motor principal) produce el movimiento: el bíceps braquial flexiona el codo. El tríceps es el antagonista.

Question: What is the antagonist of the m. quadriceps femoris during a knee extension?
Explanation (EN): The antagonist performs the opposite movement. The hamstrings flex the knee, so they oppose the quadriceps.
Explicación (ES): El antagonista realiza el movimiento opuesto. Los isquiotibiales flexionan la rodilla, por lo que se oponen al cuádriceps.

Question: Which muscle group is primarily responsible for hip extension?
Explanation (EN): The gluteus maximus and hamstrings extend the hip, for example when standing up from a squat or during a deadlift.
Explicación (ES): El glúteo mayor y los isquiotibiales extienden la cadera, por ejemplo al levantarse de una sentadilla o en el peso muerto.

Question: Which muscle is the main hip flexor?
Explanation (EN): The iliopsoas (psoas major + iliacus) is the strongest hip flexor.
Explicación (ES): El iliopsoas (psoas mayor + ilíaco) es el flexor de cadera más potente.

Question: Which part of the quadriceps also crosses the hip joint?
Explanation (EN): The rectus femoris is a two-joint (bi-articular) muscle: it extends the knee and also flexes the hip.
Explicación (ES): El recto femoral es un músculo biarticular: extiende la rodilla y además flexiona la cadera.

Question: Which muscle forms most of the calf and plantar-flexes the ankle?
Explanation (EN): The gastrocnemius (with the soleus) plantar-flexes the ankle, as in a calf raise. The tibialis anterior does the opposite (dorsiflexion).
Explicación (ES): El gastrocnemio (junto con el sóleo) realiza la flexión plantar del tobillo, como en una elevación de talones. El tibial anterior hace lo contrario (dorsiflexión).

Question: Which muscle is mainly trained with a lat pulldown?
Explanation (EN): The latissimus dorsi adducts and extends the upper arm, which is the pulling-down movement of the lat pulldown.
Explicación (ES): El dorsal ancho aduce y extiende el brazo, que es el movimiento de tirar hacia abajo en el jalón al pecho.

Question: Which muscle keeps the spine upright and extends the back?
Explanation (EN): The erector spinae runs along the spine and extends it; it is important for posture.
Explicación (ES): El erector de la columna recorre la columna vertebral y la extiende; es importante para la postura.

Question: Which abdominal muscle acts like a natural 'corset' and is important for core stability?
Explanation (EN): The transversus abdominis is the deepest abdominal muscle; it wraps around the trunk and raises intra-abdominal pressure to stabilise the spine.
Explicación (ES): El transverso del abdomen es el músculo abdominal más profundo; rodea el tronco y aumenta la presión intraabdominal para estabilizar la columna.

Question: What connects a muscle to a bone?
Explanation (EN): Tendons connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone.
Explicación (ES): Los tendones conectan el músculo con el hueso. Los ligamentos conectan hueso con hueso.

Question: What connects bone to bone and stabilises a joint?
Explanation (EN): Ligaments connect bones to each other and give stability to joints.
Explicación (ES): Los ligamentos unen los huesos entre sí y dan estabilidad a las articulaciones.

Question: How many vertebrae does the cervical spine have?
Explanation (EN): Cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, then the sacrum and coccyx.
Explicación (ES): Cervicales 7, torácicas 12, lumbares 5, después el sacro y el cóccix.

Question: How many thoracic vertebrae are there?
Explanation (EN): There are 12 thoracic vertebrae; each connects to a pair of ribs.
Explicación (ES): Hay 12 vértebras torácicas; cada una se une a un par de costillas.

Question: The natural forward curve of the lumbar spine is called...
Explanation (EN): Lordosis is the natural inward (forward) curve in the neck and lower back. Kyphosis is the outward curve of the thoracic spine. Scoliosis is a sideways curve.
Explicación (ES): La lordosis es la curva natural hacia dentro (hacia delante) del cuello y la zona lumbar. La cifosis es la curva hacia fuera de la columna torácica. La escoliosis es una curva lateral.

Question: An abnormal sideways curvature of the spine is called...
Explanation (EN): Scoliosis is a lateral (sideways) curvature of the spine, often with rotation.
Explicación (ES): La escoliosis es una curvatura lateral de la columna, a menudo con rotación.

Question: What is the longest and strongest bone in the human body?
Explanation (EN): The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone.
Explicación (ES): El fémur (hueso del muslo) es el hueso más largo y fuerte.

Question: Which muscle fibre type is best suited for endurance activities?
Explanation (EN): Type I (slow-twitch, red) fibres have many mitochondria and capillaries, use oxygen and fatigue slowly.
Explicación (ES): Las fibras tipo I (lentas, rojas) tienen muchas mitocondrias y capilares, usan oxígeno y se fatigan lentamente.

Question: Which statement about type II (fast-twitch) muscle fibres is correct?
B: They produce a lot of force quickly but fatigue fast
D: They are mainly used at rest
Explanation (EN): Fast-twitch fibres contract quickly and forcefully, rely more on anaerobic energy and tire quickly. Sprinters have a high proportion.
Explicación (ES): Las fibras rápidas se contraen con rapidez y fuerza, dependen más de la energía anaeróbica y se cansan pronto. Los velocistas tienen una gran proporción.

Question: A muscle contraction in which the muscle lengthens under tension is called...
Explanation (EN): Eccentric = lengthening under load (e.g. lowering the bar in a curl). Concentric = shortening. Isometric = no change in length.
Explicación (ES): Excéntrica = alargamiento bajo carga (p. ej., bajar la barra en un curl). Concéntrica = acortamiento. Isométrica = sin cambio de longitud.

Question: Holding a plank is an example of which type of muscle contraction?
Explanation (EN): In an isometric contraction the muscle produces force without changing length and without joint movement.
Explicación (ES): En una contracción isométrica el músculo produce fuerza sin cambiar de longitud y sin movimiento articular.

Question: Turning the palm of the hand downward is called...
Explanation (EN): Pronation turns the palm down (or back). Supination turns the palm up, as if holding a bowl of soup.
Explicación (ES): La pronación gira la palma hacia abajo (o atrás). La supinación gira la palma hacia arriba, como si sostuvieras un plato de sopa.

Question: Which term describes a position closer to the trunk or point of attachment?
Explanation (EN): Proximal = closer to the trunk/origin; distal = further away. The elbow is proximal to the wrist.
Explicación (ES): Proximal = más cerca del tronco/origen; distal = más lejos. El codo es proximal respecto a la muñeca.

Question: Where in the body are red blood cells produced?
Explanation (EN): Red blood cells are produced in the red bone marrow (haematopoiesis), one of the functions of the skeleton.
Explicación (ES): Los glóbulos rojos se producen en la médula ósea roja (hematopoyesis), una de las funciones del esqueleto.

Question: Which joint type allows the most freedom of movement?
Explanation (EN): Ball-and-socket joints (shoulder, hip) move in all three planes, so they have the largest range of motion.
Explicación (ES): Las articulaciones esféricas (hombro, cadera) se mueven en los tres planos, por lo que tienen la mayor amplitud de movimiento.

Question: EPOC stands for
Explanation (EN): EPOC = Excess Post-exercise Oxygen Consumption: the extra oxygen used after exercise to restore the body (refill CP stores, clear lactate, cool down). Note the trap words 'Extra' and the missing 'consumption'.
Explicación (ES): EPOC = consumo excesivo de oxígeno post-ejercicio: el oxígeno extra que se usa después del ejercicio para recuperar el cuerpo (reponer la fosfocreatina, eliminar lactato, enfriarse). Cuidado con las trampas 'Extra' y la falta de 'consumption'.

Question: What is ADP?
D: A residue after cleavage of ATP
Explanation (EN): When ATP releases energy, one phosphate group splits off and ADP (adenosine diphosphate) remains. ADP is then rebuilt into ATP.
Explicación (ES): Cuando el ATP libera energía, se separa un grupo fosfato y queda ADP (adenosín difosfato). Después el ADP se vuelve a convertir en ATP.

Question: What substance is produced during the anaerobic breakdown of glucose in the muscle fibre?
Explanation (EN): Without enough oxygen, glucose is broken down to pyruvate and then lactic acid (lactate). CO2 and H2O are the products of aerobic breakdown.
Explicación (ES): Sin suficiente oxígeno, la glucosa se descompone en piruvato y luego en ácido láctico (lactato). El CO2 y el H2O son los productos de la vía aeróbica.

Question: What is ATP?
A: The direct energy source for muscle contraction
C: A hormone that regulates blood sugar
D: A waste product of fat burning
Explanation (EN): ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the only direct energy source for muscle contraction. All energy systems exist to rebuild ATP.
Explicación (ES): El ATP (adenosín trifosfato) es la única fuente directa de energía para la contracción muscular. Todos los sistemas energéticos existen para regenerar ATP.

Question: How long does the ATP-CP (phosphagen) system supply energy at maximal effort?
Explanation (EN): Stored ATP and creatine phosphate deliver energy very fast but only for roughly 6–10 seconds of maximal effort, e.g. a 60 m sprint or a heavy single lift.
Explicación (ES): El ATP almacenado y la fosfocreatina aportan energía muy rápido pero solo durante unos 6–10 segundos de esfuerzo máximo, p. ej., un sprint de 60 m o un levantamiento pesado.

Question: Which energy system dominates during a 400 m sprint (about 50–60 seconds)?
Explanation (EN): Maximal efforts of roughly 10 seconds to 2 minutes rely mainly on anaerobic glycolysis, which produces lactate.
Explicación (ES): Los esfuerzos máximos de unos 10 segundos a 2 minutos dependen sobre todo de la glucólisis anaeróbica, que produce lactato.

Question: Which energy system is used mainly during a 45-minute easy run?
Explanation (EN): Long, moderate efforts are fuelled aerobically: carbohydrates and fats are broken down with oxygen in the mitochondria.
Explicación (ES): Los esfuerzos largos y moderados se alimentan aeróbicamente: los carbohidratos y las grasas se descomponen con oxígeno en las mitocondrias.

Question: What are the end products of the aerobic breakdown of glucose?
Explanation (EN): With oxygen, glucose is fully broken down to carbon dioxide, water and a large amount of ATP.
Explicación (ES): Con oxígeno, la glucosa se descompone por completo en dióxido de carbono, agua y una gran cantidad de ATP.

Question: In which part of the muscle cell does aerobic energy production take place?
Explanation (EN): The mitochondria are the 'power plants' of the cell, where aerobic ATP production takes place.
Explicación (ES): Las mitocondrias son las 'centrales eléctricas' de la célula, donde se produce el ATP de forma aeróbica.

Question: Which energy system delivers energy the fastest?
Explanation (EN): The ATP-CP system is the fastest (one chemical step) but has the smallest capacity. The aerobic system is the slowest but has the largest capacity.
Explicación (ES): El sistema ATP-PC es el más rápido (un solo paso químico) pero tiene la menor capacidad. El sistema aeróbico es el más lento pero tiene la mayor capacidad.

Question: What does VO2max indicate?
D: Maximum amount of oxygen the body can take up and use per minute
Explanation (EN): VO2max is the maximal oxygen uptake (ml/kg/min), the best single indicator of aerobic (cardiorespiratory) fitness.
Explicación (ES): El VO2max es el consumo máximo de oxígeno (ml/kg/min), el mejor indicador individual de la capacidad aeróbica (cardiorrespiratoria).

Question: Which formula is commonly used to estimate maximum heart rate?
Explanation (EN): HRmax ≈ 220 − age. It is an estimate with a spread of about ±10–12 beats.
Explicación (ES): FCmáx ≈ 220 − edad. Es una estimación con un margen de unos ±10–12 latidos.

Question: Cardiac output is...
Explanation (EN): Cardiac output (litres per minute) = heart rate × stroke volume (the amount of blood pumped per beat).
Explicación (ES): El gasto cardíaco (litros por minuto) = frecuencia cardíaca × volumen sistólico (la cantidad de sangre bombeada por latido).

Question: What is a typical long-term effect of endurance training on resting heart rate?
Explanation (EN): Endurance training enlarges the stroke volume, so the heart needs fewer beats at rest to pump the same amount of blood.
Explicación (ES): El entrenamiento de resistencia aumenta el volumen sistólico, así que el corazón necesita menos latidos en reposo para bombear la misma cantidad de sangre.

Question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
Explanation (EN): Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back. Gas exchange takes place in the capillaries.
Explicación (ES): Las arterias llevan la sangre desde el corazón; las venas la devuelven. El intercambio de gases ocurre en los capilares.

Question: Where does gas exchange between the lungs and the blood take place?
Explanation (EN): Oxygen and CO2 are exchanged in the alveoli, tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries.
Explicación (ES): El oxígeno y el CO2 se intercambian en los alvéolos, pequeños sacos de aire rodeados de capilares.

Question: What is the main breathing muscle?
Explanation (EN): The diaphragm contracts and flattens during inhalation, which draws air into the lungs.
Explicación (ES): El diafragma se contrae y se aplana durante la inspiración, lo que hace entrar aire en los pulmones.

Question: Which substance in the blood transports oxygen?
Explanation (EN): Haemoglobin in the red blood cells binds oxygen and carries it to the tissues.
Explicación (ES): La hemoglobina de los glóbulos rojos se une al oxígeno y lo transporta a los tejidos.

Question: What is the anaerobic (lactate) threshold?
B: The point at which fat burning stops completely
C: The intensity above which lactate builds up faster than it can be removed
D: The maximum amount of weight you can lift
Explanation (EN): Above the lactate threshold, lactate production exceeds clearance, so it accumulates and fatigue follows quickly.
Explicación (ES): Por encima del umbral de lactato, la producción supera la eliminación, el lactato se acumula y la fatiga llega rápido.

Question: In which form are carbohydrates stored in the muscles and liver?
Explanation (EN): Carbohydrate is stored as glycogen in muscle and liver. Fat is stored as triglycerides.
Explicación (ES): Los carbohidratos se almacenan como glucógeno en el músculo y el hígado. La grasa se almacena como triglicéridos.

Question: Which hormone lowers blood sugar levels?
Explanation (EN): Insulin (from the pancreas) helps cells take up glucose, which lowers blood sugar. Glucagon raises it.
Explicación (ES): La insulina (del páncreas) ayuda a las células a absorber la glucosa, lo que reduce el azúcar en sangre. El glucagón lo eleva.

Question: What is supercompensation?
A: Eating extra carbohydrates before a match
B: Overtraining caused by too little rest
D: Recovery to a level above the starting level after training and rest
Explanation (EN): After training load (fatigue) and adequate recovery, the body adapts above its previous level. Training again at that moment leads to progress.
Explicación (ES): Tras la carga de entrenamiento (fatiga) y una recuperación adecuada, el cuerpo se adapta por encima de su nivel anterior. Volver a entrenar en ese momento produce progreso.

Question: What is the main cause of muscle hypertrophy?
C: An increase in the size (cross-section) of existing muscle fibres
D: An increase in the number of muscle fibres
Explanation (EN): Hypertrophy mainly means existing fibres get thicker through more myofibrils and contractile proteins.
Explicación (ES): La hipertrofia significa principalmente que las fibras existentes se engrosan por un aumento de miofibrillas y proteínas contráctiles.

Question: Strength gains in the first weeks of a strength training programme are mainly caused by...
Explanation (EN): Early gains (roughly the first 4–8 weeks) come mainly from the nervous system: more motor units recruited and better coordination. Hypertrophy follows later.
Explicación (ES): Las mejoras iniciales (aproximadamente las primeras 4–8 semanas) vienen sobre todo del sistema nervioso: se reclutan más unidades motoras y mejora la coordinación. La hipertrofia llega después.

Question: A motor unit consists of...
B: The brain and the spinal cord
C: One motor neuron and all the muscle fibres it innervates
Explanation (EN): A motor unit is one motor neuron plus all the muscle fibres it controls. More force = more and larger motor units recruited.
Explicación (ES): Una unidad motora es una motoneurona más todas las fibras musculares que controla. Más fuerza = se reclutan más unidades motoras y más grandes.

Question: Which statement about lactate (lactic acid) is correct?
A: It is only produced at rest
B: It is produced during anaerobic glycolysis and can be reused as fuel
C: It is produced in the ATP-CP system
D: It causes muscle soreness 2 days after training (DOMS)
Explanation (EN): Lactate is a by-product of anaerobic glycolysis and is reused as fuel (by the heart, muscles and liver). DOMS is caused by micro-damage, not lactate.
Explicación (ES): El lactato es un subproducto de la glucólisis anaeróbica y se reutiliza como combustible (corazón, músculos, hígado). Las agujetas (DOMS) se deben a microlesiones, no al lactato.

Question: What is DOMS?
Explanation (EN): DOMS = Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness, the stiffness that peaks 24–72 hours after unaccustomed (especially eccentric) exercise.
Explicación (ES): DOMS = dolor muscular de aparición tardía (agujetas), la rigidez que alcanza su máximo 24–72 horas después de un ejercicio no habitual (sobre todo excéntrico).

Question: Which type of contraction causes the most muscle soreness (DOMS)?
Explanation (EN): Eccentric contractions (e.g. downhill running, lowering weights) cause the most micro-damage and therefore the most DOMS.
Explicación (ES): Las contracciones excéntricas (p. ej., correr cuesta abajo, bajar pesos) causan más microlesiones y, por tanto, más agujetas.

Question: What is the normal resting heart rate range for an adult?
Explanation (EN): Normal resting heart rate is about 60–100 beats per minute. Well-trained endurance athletes can be lower.
Explicación (ES): La frecuencia cardíaca normal en reposo es de unos 60–100 latidos por minuto. Los deportistas de resistencia entrenados pueden tenerla más baja.

Question: Which blood pressure value is considered normal/optimal for adults?
Explanation (EN): Around 120/80 mmHg (systolic/diastolic) is normal. 140/90 or higher is generally classed as high blood pressure (hypertension).
Explicación (ES): Alrededor de 120/80 mmHg (sistólica/diastólica) es normal. 140/90 o más se clasifica generalmente como hipertensión.

Question: The systolic blood pressure is the pressure...
Explanation (EN): Systolic = pressure during contraction of the heart (upper number). Diastolic = pressure during relaxation (lower number).
Explicación (ES): Sistólica = presión durante la contracción del corazón (número superior). Diastólica = presión durante la relajación (número inferior).

Question: Which macronutrient is the main fuel at rest and during low-intensity exercise?
Explanation (EN): At rest and low intensity, fat supplies most of the energy. As intensity rises, carbohydrate takes over.
Explicación (ES): En reposo y a baja intensidad, la grasa aporta la mayor parte de la energía. Al aumentar la intensidad, los carbohidratos toman el relevo.

Question: What happens to blood flow to the working muscles during exercise?
Explanation (EN): During exercise blood is redirected to working muscles (vasodilation there, less to the digestive organs).
Explicación (ES): Durante el ejercicio la sangre se redirige a los músculos activos (vasodilatación allí y menos flujo a los órganos digestivos).

Question: Creatine phosphate is used to...
Explanation (EN): Creatine phosphate donates its phosphate to ADP, rebuilding ATP very quickly at the start of intense effort.
Explicación (ES): La fosfocreatina cede su fosfato al ADP y regenera ATP muy rápidamente al inicio de un esfuerzo intenso.

Question: The definition of biomechanics is?
A: Indicating the difference between strength, load and being strong
B: Calculating the magnitude and direction of the force
C: Creating training schedules with the help of different forces
D: The doctrine of forces and the effect of forces on the human body
Explanation (EN): Biomechanics is the study of forces and their effects on the human body (movement, loading of joints and tissues).
Explicación (ES): La biomecánica es el estudio de las fuerzas y sus efectos sobre el cuerpo humano (movimiento, carga de articulaciones y tejidos).

Question: How does overloading occur?
A: The load is equal to the load capacity
B: The load is higher than the load capacity
C: The load capacity is greater than the load
D: The load is lower than the load capacity
Explanation (EN): Overload (overbelasting) happens when the load is greater than what the tissue or person can handle (the load capacity). This can lead to injury.
Explicación (ES): La sobrecarga ocurre cuando la carga es mayor que lo que el tejido o la persona puede soportar (la capacidad de carga). Puede provocar lesiones.

Question: What is load capacity (belastbaarheid)?
A: The total training volume per week
C: The number of repetitions in a set
D: The amount of load a person or tissue can handle without damage
Explanation (EN): Load capacity is what the body or a tissue can tolerate. Good training keeps load slightly above current level, then lets capacity grow with recovery.
Explicación (ES): La capacidad de carga es lo que el cuerpo o un tejido puede tolerar. Un buen entrenamiento mantiene la carga ligeramente por encima del nivel actual y deja que la capacidad crezca con la recuperación.

Question: Which factor lowers a person's load capacity?
Explanation (EN): Fatigue, stress, poor sleep, illness and previous injury reduce load capacity, so the same load is more likely to cause overload.
Explicación (ES): La fatiga, el estrés, dormir mal, la enfermedad y las lesiones previas reducen la capacidad de carga, así que la misma carga tiene más probabilidad de causar sobrecarga.

Question: A force is described by its...
B: Size (magnitude), direction and point of application
Explanation (EN): A force is a vector: it has a magnitude, a direction and a point of application.
Explicación (ES): Una fuerza es un vector: tiene magnitud, dirección y punto de aplicación.

Question: In what unit is force expressed?
Explanation (EN): Force is measured in Newtons (N). 1 kg of mass weighs roughly 10 N on Earth.
Explicación (ES): La fuerza se mide en newtons (N). 1 kg de masa pesa aproximadamente 10 N en la Tierra.

Question: Newton's second law states that...
B: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
D: An object stays at rest unless a force acts on it
Explanation (EN): F = m × a. The first law is inertia; the third is action = reaction.
Explicación (ES): F = m × a. La primera ley es la inercia; la tercera es acción = reacción.

Question: When you push off the ground while running, the ground pushes back on you. Which law is this?
Explanation (EN): Newton's third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction (ground reaction force).
Explicación (ES): Tercera ley de Newton: a toda acción le corresponde una reacción igual y opuesta (fuerza de reacción del suelo).

Question: What is a moment (torque)?
Explanation (EN): Moment (torque) = force × moment arm (the perpendicular distance from the line of force to the axis of rotation).
Explicación (ES): El momento (par de fuerza) = fuerza × brazo de momento (la distancia perpendicular de la línea de fuerza al eje de rotación).

Question: During a lateral raise, when is the load on the shoulder greatest?
C: The load is the same throughout
D: At the start of the movement
Explanation (EN): The moment arm of the dumbbell is longest when the arm is horizontal, so the torque on the shoulder is highest there.
Explicación (ES): El brazo de momento de la mancuerna es máximo cuando el brazo está horizontal, por lo que el par sobre el hombro es mayor en ese punto.

Question: How can you make a push-up easier without changing the exercise?
C: Do it from the knees (shorter lever)
D: Put the feet on a bench
Explanation (EN): From the knees the lever (body length) is shorter and less body weight is lifted, which lowers the load.
Explicación (ES): Desde las rodillas la palanca (longitud del cuerpo) es más corta y se levanta menos peso corporal, lo que reduce la carga.

Question: In a squat, which change increases the load (moment) on the lower back?
Explanation (EN): Leaning forward moves the bar further from the hip and spine axis, so the moment arm and the load on the lower back increase.
Explicación (ES): Inclinarse hacia delante aleja la barra del eje de la cadera y la columna, de modo que aumentan el brazo de momento y la carga en la zona lumbar.

Question: A lever system consists of...
Explanation (EN): Every lever has an axis/fulcrum (the joint), an effort (muscle force) and a resistance (load). In the body, bones are the levers.
Explicación (ES): Toda palanca tiene un eje o punto de apoyo (la articulación), una potencia (fuerza muscular) y una resistencia (carga). En el cuerpo, los huesos son las palancas.

Question: Most levers in the human body (e.g. the elbow during a biceps curl) are...
Explanation (EN): In a third-class lever the effort lies between the axis and the load. This favours speed and range of motion over force.
Explicación (ES): En una palanca de tercer grado la potencia está entre el eje y la carga. Favorece la velocidad y la amplitud de movimiento frente a la fuerza.

Question: Standing on your toes (calf raise) is often given as an example of a...
Explanation (EN): In a calf raise the axis is the ball of the foot, the load (body weight) is in the middle and the effort (calf) is at the heel: a second-class lever.
Explicación (ES): En una elevación de talones el eje es la parte anterior del pie, la carga (peso corporal) está en el medio y la potencia (gemelo) en el talón: palanca de segundo grado.

Question: Nodding the head (the neck joint as axis between head weight and neck muscles) is an example of a...
Explanation (EN): In a first-class lever the axis lies between effort and load, like a seesaw.
Explicación (ES): En una palanca de primer grado el eje está entre la potencia y la carga, como un balancín.

Question: When is a person most stable?
A: Large base of support and low centre of gravity
B: Small base of support and high centre of gravity
D: Centre of gravity outside the base of support
Explanation (EN): Stability increases with a wider base of support, a lower centre of gravity and the centre of gravity well within the base.
Explicación (ES): La estabilidad aumenta con una base de apoyo más amplia, un centro de gravedad más bajo y el centro de gravedad bien dentro de la base.

Question: Where is the centre of gravity of a standing adult roughly located?
A: At the level of the head
B: Around the navel / just in front of the sacrum
Explanation (EN): In upright standing the centre of gravity lies roughly at navel height, just in front of the second sacral vertebra.
Explicación (ES): De pie, el centro de gravedad está aproximadamente a la altura del ombligo, justo delante de la segunda vértebra sacra.

Question: Which type of load on tissue is caused by forces pulling in opposite directions?
Explanation (EN): Tension pulls tissue apart; compression pushes it together; shear makes layers slide; torsion twists.
Explicación (ES): La tensión (tracción) separa el tejido; la compresión lo junta; el cizallamiento hace deslizar las capas; la torsión lo retuerce.

Question: Speed × mass equals...
Explanation (EN): Momentum = mass × velocity. Power = work ÷ time. Work = force × distance.
Explicación (ES): Cantidad de movimiento = masa × velocidad. Potencia = trabajo ÷ tiempo. Trabajo = fuerza × distancia.

Question: Power is defined as...
Explanation (EN): Power is the rate of doing work: work ÷ time, or force × velocity. Explosive movements require high power.
Explicación (ES): La potencia es la rapidez con la que se realiza un trabajo: trabajo ÷ tiempo, o fuerza × velocidad. Los movimientos explosivos requieren mucha potencia.

Question: Why does a cable machine give a different strength curve than a free weight?
B: The direction of resistance follows the cable, not gravity
C: Gravity always pulls the cable down
Explanation (EN): With free weights resistance always acts vertically (gravity). With cables, resistance follows the cable line, so the hardest point of the movement changes.
Explicación (ES): Con peso libre la resistencia siempre actúa en vertical (gravedad). Con poleas, la resistencia sigue la línea del cable, así que el punto más difícil del movimiento cambia.

Question: What is the effect of a longer lever arm with the same weight?
Explanation (EN): Torque = force × lever arm. Longer arm, same weight → more torque, so the exercise feels heavier (e.g. straight-arm vs bent-arm fly).
Explicación (ES): Par = fuerza × brazo de palanca. Brazo más largo con el mismo peso → más par, así que el ejercicio se siente más pesado (p. ej., aperturas con brazos rectos frente a flexionados).

Question: Load and load capacity are in balance. What happens if you train regularly with a load slightly above the current capacity and allow recovery?
Explanation (EN): A load slightly above capacity followed by recovery stimulates adaptation, so load capacity grows (principle of progressive overload).
Explicación (ES): Una carga ligeramente superior a la capacidad seguida de recuperación estimula la adaptación, así que la capacidad de carga aumenta (principio de sobrecarga progresiva).

Question: Which statement about friction is correct?
B: Friction is a force that opposes sliding between two surfaces
Explanation (EN): Friction resists sliding between surfaces. Good shoe grip uses friction; a slippery floor lacks it.
Explicación (ES): La fricción se opone al deslizamiento entre superficies. El buen agarre de una zapatilla usa la fricción; un suelo resbaladizo carece de ella.

Question: A deadlift with the bar far from the shins is riskier because...
D: The moment arm to the lower back increases
Explanation (EN): The further the bar is from the body, the longer the moment arm around the hip and spine, which increases load on the lower back.
Explicación (ES): Cuanto más lejos esté la barra del cuerpo, más largo es el brazo de momento alrededor de la cadera y la columna, lo que aumenta la carga en la zona lumbar.

Question: What is inertia?
A: The speed of a falling object
C: The tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion
Explanation (EN): Inertia (Newton's first law): an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless a force acts on it. More mass = more inertia.
Explicación (ES): Inercia (primera ley de Newton): un objeto permanece en reposo o en movimiento uniforme a menos que actúe una fuerza sobre él. Más masa = más inercia.

Question: What is a closed kinetic chain exercise?
A: An exercise in which the hand or foot moves freely (e.g. leg extension)
B: An exercise performed on a machine only
D: An exercise in which the hand or foot is fixed against a surface (e.g. squat, push-up)
Explanation (EN): Closed chain: distal segment fixed (squat, push-up). Open chain: distal segment free (leg extension, biceps curl).
Explicación (ES): Cadena cerrada: segmento distal fijo (sentadilla, flexión). Cadena abierta: segmento distal libre (extensión de pierna, curl de bíceps).

Question: A leg extension on a machine is an example of...
Explanation (EN): In a leg extension the foot moves freely, so it is an open kinetic chain exercise.
Explicación (ES): En una extensión de pierna el pie se mueve libremente, así que es un ejercicio de cadena cinética abierta.

Question: What does the training principle 'specificity' mean?
A: You should always train with heavy weights
B: Training must be varied every session
C: Every training gives the same result
D: The body adapts specifically to the type of load it is given
Explanation (EN): Specificity: adaptations match the training stimulus. A marathon runner should mainly train endurance, not maximal strength.
Explicación (ES): Especificidad: las adaptaciones corresponden al estímulo de entrenamiento. Un maratoniano debe entrenar sobre todo la resistencia, no la fuerza máxima.

Question: What does the principle of 'reversibility' mean?
A: Exercises can be done in reverse order
B: Training effects disappear when training stops
C: Heavier training always gives faster results
D: You can reverse an injury by training
Explanation (EN): Reversibility ('use it or lose it'): when you stop training, adaptations gradually decline.
Explicación (ES): Reversibilidad ('lo que no se usa se pierde'): cuando dejas de entrenar, las adaptaciones disminuyen poco a poco.

Question: What does 'progressive overload' mean?
B: Training more than twice a day
C: Gradually increasing the training load as the body adapts
Explanation (EN): Progressive overload: increase load (weight, reps, sets, intensity, duration) step by step to keep stimulating adaptation.
Explicación (ES): Sobrecarga progresiva: aumentar la carga (peso, repeticiones, series, intensidad, duración) poco a poco para seguir estimulando la adaptación.

Question: What does FITT stand for?
Explanation (EN): FITT = Frequency, Intensity, Time (duration), Type. These are the variables you adjust in a training programme.
Explicación (ES): FITT = Frecuencia, Intensidad, Tiempo (duración), Tipo. Son las variables que se ajustan en un programa de entrenamiento.

Question: Which repetition range is most suitable for training maximal strength?
Explanation (EN): Maximal strength is trained with heavy loads (about 85%+ of 1RM) for 1–5 reps and long rests.
Explicación (ES): La fuerza máxima se entrena con cargas altas (aprox. 85%+ del 1RM) en 1–5 repeticiones y descansos largos.

Question: Which repetition range is classically recommended for hypertrophy (muscle growth)?
Explanation (EN): The classic hypertrophy zone is about 6–12 reps at roughly 65–85% of 1RM, with moderate rests (about 60–90 s).
Explicación (ES): La zona clásica de hipertrofia es de unas 6–12 repeticiones al 65–85% del 1RM, con descansos moderados (unos 60–90 s).

Question: Which repetition range fits muscular endurance training?
Explanation (EN): Muscular endurance is trained with lighter loads (below about 65% 1RM) and high reps (15+), with short rests.
Explicación (ES): La resistencia muscular se entrena con cargas ligeras (por debajo del 65% del 1RM) y muchas repeticiones (15+), con descansos cortos.

Question: What does 1RM mean?
A: The maximum weight you can lift once with good technique
C: The minimum weight for a warm-up
Explanation (EN): 1RM (one repetition maximum) is the heaviest load you can lift for a single correct repetition. Training loads are often given as a % of 1RM.
Explicación (ES): El 1RM (una repetición máxima) es la carga más pesada que puedes levantar en una sola repetición correcta. Las cargas suelen expresarse como % del 1RM.

Question: What rest between sets is appropriate for maximal strength training?
Explanation (EN): Heavy maximal strength sets need 2–5 minutes so the ATP-CP system can recover.
Explicación (ES): Las series pesadas de fuerza máxima necesitan 2–5 minutos para que el sistema ATP-PC se recupere.

Question: What is periodisation?
C: Systematically planning training in phases (cycles) with different goals
D: Training at the same intensity all year
Explanation (EN): Periodisation divides training into macro-, meso- and microcycles with changing goals, volume and intensity to optimise progress and prevent overtraining.
Explicación (ES): La periodización divide el entrenamiento en macro-, meso- y microciclos con objetivos, volumen e intensidad cambiantes para optimizar el progreso y evitar el sobreentrenamiento.

Question: A microcycle usually lasts...
Explanation (EN): Microcycle ≈ 1 week; mesocycle ≈ several weeks (often 3–6); macrocycle ≈ a season or a year.
Explicación (ES): Microciclo ≈ 1 semana; mesociclo ≈ varias semanas (a menudo 3–6); macrociclo ≈ una temporada o un año.

Question: What is the order of the training cycles from largest to smallest?
Explanation (EN): Macro (largest, e.g. a year) → meso (block of weeks) → micro (a week).
Explicación (ES): Macro (el más grande, p. ej., un año) → meso (bloque de semanas) → micro (una semana).

Question: Which is a sign of overtraining?
B: Persistent fatigue, declining performance and a raised resting heart rate
D: Lower resting heart rate and better sleep
Explanation (EN): Overtraining shows as lasting fatigue, falling performance, raised resting heart rate, poor sleep, irritability and more illness.
Explicación (ES): El sobreentrenamiento se manifiesta como fatiga persistente, bajada del rendimiento, frecuencia cardíaca en reposo elevada, mal sueño, irritabilidad y más enfermedades.

Question: The Karvonen formula uses...
Explanation (EN): Karvonen: target HR = HRrest + (HRmax − HRrest) × intensity %. It accounts for individual resting heart rate.
Explicación (ES): Karvonen: FC objetivo = FCreposo + (FCmáx − FCreposo) × % de intensidad. Tiene en cuenta la frecuencia cardíaca en reposo individual.

Question: A 40-year-old client has a resting heart rate of 60. Using Karvonen, what is the target heart rate at 70% intensity?
Explanation (EN): HRmax = 220 − 40 = 180. Reserve = 180 − 60 = 120. 120 × 0.7 = 84. Target = 60 + 84 = 144 bpm. (126 bpm is 70% of HRmax, the simple method without the resting heart rate.)

Question: What does RPE stand for?
Explanation (EN): RPE = Rate (Rating) of Perceived Exertion, e.g. the Borg scale (6–20) or a 1–10 scale.
Explicación (ES): RPE = escala de esfuerzo percibido, p. ej., la escala de Borg (6–20) o una escala de 1–10.

Question: The original Borg scale runs from...
Explanation (EN): The original Borg RPE scale runs from 6 to 20 (roughly heart rate ÷ 10). The modified CR10 scale runs from 0 to 10.
Explicación (ES): La escala de Borg original va de 6 a 20 (aproximadamente frecuencia cardíaca ÷ 10). La escala CR10 modificada va de 0 a 10.

Question: What is interval training?
D: Alternating periods of high intensity with periods of rest or low intensity
Explanation (EN): Interval training alternates work and recovery bouts, allowing more time at high intensity than continuous training.
Explicación (ES): El entrenamiento por intervalos alterna fases de trabajo y recuperación, lo que permite pasar más tiempo a alta intensidad que el entrenamiento continuo.

Question: What is circuit training?
B: A series of exercises done one after another with little rest
Explanation (EN): Circuit training: several stations performed in sequence with short rests, often combining strength and cardio.
Explicación (ES): El entrenamiento en circuito: varias estaciones realizadas en secuencia con descansos cortos, a menudo combinando fuerza y cardio.

Question: What is a superset?
C: Two exercises performed back to back without rest, often for opposing muscle groups
Explanation (EN): A superset combines two exercises without rest in between, often agonist and antagonist (e.g. biceps curl + triceps extension).
Explicación (ES): Una superserie combina dos ejercicios sin descanso entre ellos, a menudo agonista y antagonista (p. ej., curl de bíceps + extensión de tríceps).

Question: What is the main purpose of a warm-up?
A: To burn as many calories as possible
B: To tire the muscles before training
D: To prepare body and mind for exercise and reduce injury risk
Explanation (EN): A warm-up raises body and muscle temperature and heart rate, improves mobility and coordination, and prepares mentally.
Explicación (ES): El calentamiento eleva la temperatura corporal y muscular y la frecuencia cardíaca, mejora la movilidad y la coordinación y prepara mentalmente.

Question: How long should a general warm-up typically last?
Explanation (EN): A typical warm-up lasts about 5–15 minutes, longer in cold conditions or before intense efforts.
Explicación (ES): Un calentamiento típico dura unos 5–15 minutos, más en condiciones frías o antes de esfuerzos intensos.

Question: Which type of stretching is best suited to a warm-up?
Explanation (EN): Dynamic stretching (controlled movements through the range) prepares muscles without the temporary drop in strength that long static holds can cause.
Explicación (ES): El estiramiento dinámico (movimientos controlados en todo el rango) prepara los músculos sin la pérdida temporal de fuerza que pueden provocar los estiramientos estáticos largos.

Question: What is the purpose of a cool-down?
D: To gradually bring heart rate and breathing back to rest
Explanation (EN): A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate and breathing and helps avoid blood pooling and dizziness after intense exercise.
Explicación (ES): La vuelta a la calma reduce poco a poco la frecuencia cardíaca y la respiración y ayuda a evitar la acumulación de sangre y los mareos tras un ejercicio intenso.

Question: What does PNF stretching stand for?
Explanation (EN): PNF = Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation: contract-relax techniques to increase range of motion.
Explicación (ES): PNF = Facilitación Neuromuscular Propioceptiva: técnicas de contracción-relajación para aumentar la amplitud de movimiento.

Question: How long is a static stretch typically held to improve flexibility?
Explanation (EN): Hold static stretches about 15–30 seconds (up to 60 for older adults), to mild tension, never pain.
Explicación (ES): Mantén los estiramientos estáticos unos 15–30 segundos (hasta 60 en personas mayores), hasta una tensión leve, nunca dolor.

Question: What is the recommended minimum amount of moderate-intensity physical activity for adults per week (WHO)?
Explanation (EN): WHO: at least 150–300 minutes of moderate (or 75–150 min vigorous) activity per week, plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days.
Explicación (ES): OMS: al menos 150–300 minutos de actividad moderada (o 75–150 min vigorosa) por semana, más ejercicios de fortalecimiento muscular 2 o más días.

Question: How often per week does the WHO recommend muscle-strengthening activities for adults?
Explanation (EN): Adults should do muscle-strengthening activities involving all major muscle groups on 2 or more days a week.
Explicación (ES): Los adultos deben realizar actividades de fortalecimiento de todos los grupos musculares principales 2 o más días a la semana.

Question: In a training programme, in which order should exercises usually be performed?
A: Small muscle groups first, then large
D: Large, multi-joint exercises first, then small, single-joint exercises
Explanation (EN): Do complex multi-joint exercises (squat, deadlift) while fresh, then smaller isolation exercises.
Explicación (ES): Haz los ejercicios complejos multiarticulares (sentadilla, peso muerto) cuando estás fresco y después los ejercicios de aislamiento más pequeños.

Question: Which is an example of a compound (multi-joint) exercise?
Explanation (EN): A squat involves hip, knee and ankle. A biceps curl, leg extension and calf raise involve one joint each.
Explicación (ES): La sentadilla implica cadera, rodilla y tobillo. El curl de bíceps, la extensión de pierna y la elevación de talones implican una sola articulación cada uno.

Question: What is the minimum recovery time usually advised before training the same muscle group heavily again?
Explanation (EN): After an intensive session a muscle group generally needs about 48 hours (48–72) to recover.
Explicación (ES): Tras una sesión intensa, un grupo muscular necesita en general unas 48 horas (48–72) para recuperarse.

Question: What does 'tempo 3-1-1' in strength training typically mean?
A: 3 seconds eccentric, 1 second pause, 1 second concentric
Explanation (EN): Tempo notation describes the seconds per phase, usually starting with the eccentric (lowering) phase.
Explicación (ES): La notación de tempo describe los segundos por fase, normalmente empezando por la fase excéntrica (bajada).

Question: Which heart rate zone (as % of HRmax) is generally considered moderate intensity aerobic training?
Explanation (EN): Moderate intensity is roughly 64–76% of HRmax (ACSM). Vigorous is about 77–95%.
Explicación (ES): La intensidad moderada es aproximadamente el 64–76% de la FCmáx (ACSM). La vigorosa es aproximadamente el 77–95%.

Question: Which training method is best for improving aerobic endurance in a beginner?
Explanation (EN): Beginners build aerobic endurance safely with continuous moderate-intensity training (e.g. brisk walking, cycling, easy jogging).
Explicación (ES): Los principiantes desarrollan la resistencia aeróbica con seguridad mediante entrenamiento continuo de intensidad moderada (p. ej., caminar rápido, bici, trote suave).

Question: What is plyometric training?
B: Explosive jumping/throwing using the stretch-shortening cycle
Explanation (EN): Plyometrics use a rapid eccentric then concentric action (stretch-shortening cycle) to develop power, e.g. box jumps.
Explicación (ES): La pliometría usa una acción excéntrica rápida seguida de una concéntrica (ciclo de estiramiento-acortamiento) para desarrollar potencia, p. ej., saltos al cajón.

Question: A client wants to lose fat. Which advice is most evidence-based?
A: Create an energy deficit with a combination of nutrition, cardio and strength training
B: Sweat as much as possible in a sauna suit
C: Only do abdominal exercises to burn belly fat
D: Only train in the fat-burning zone
Explanation (EN): Fat loss requires an energy deficit. Spot reduction does not work. Strength training helps preserve muscle mass during the deficit.
Explicación (ES): La pérdida de grasa requiere un déficit energético. La reducción localizada no funciona. El entrenamiento de fuerza ayuda a conservar la masa muscular durante el déficit.

Question: Which statement about training older adults is correct?
A: They do not adapt to training anymore
B: Strength and balance training help prevent falls and preserve muscle mass
C: Strength training is dangerous for them
Explanation (EN): Older adults still adapt. Strength and balance training reduce fall risk and counter sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss).
Explicación (ES): Las personas mayores siguen adaptándose. El entrenamiento de fuerza y equilibrio reduce el riesgo de caídas y combate la sarcopenia (pérdida muscular por la edad).

Question: What is sarcopenia?
B: Age-related loss of muscle mass and strength
Explanation (EN): Sarcopenia is the age-related loss of muscle mass and strength. Loss of bone density is osteoporosis.
Explicación (ES): La sarcopenia es la pérdida de masa y fuerza muscular asociada a la edad. La pérdida de densidad ósea es la osteoporosis.

Question: What is the 'Valsalva manoeuvre'?
B: Holding your breath and pressing against a closed airway, which raises blood pressure
Explanation (EN): Breath-holding while straining strongly raises blood pressure. Clients with high blood pressure or heart problems should avoid it: breathe out during the effort.
Explicación (ES): Contener la respiración mientras se hace fuerza eleva mucho la presión arterial. Los clientes con hipertensión o problemas cardíacos deben evitarlo: espirar durante el esfuerzo.

Question: When should a client exhale during a strength exercise?
B: Only at the end of the set
Explanation (EN): Exhale during the effort (e.g. pushing the bar up), inhale during the lowering phase.
Explicación (ES): Espira durante el esfuerzo (p. ej., al empujar la barra hacia arriba) e inspira durante la fase de bajada.

Question: Which substance provides the most energy per gram?
Explanation (EN): Fat ≈ 9 kcal/g, alcohol ≈ 7 kcal/g, carbohydrate (incl. sugar) and protein ≈ 4 kcal/g.
Explicación (ES): Grasa ≈ 9 kcal/g, alcohol ≈ 7 kcal/g, carbohidratos (incl. azúcar) y proteína ≈ 4 kcal/g.

Question: What are proteins important for?
B: For building and maintaining the skeleton
D: For the maintenance of muscles, tendons and ligaments
Explanation (EN): Proteins are the building material of the body: they build and repair muscles, tendons, ligaments, enzymes and hormones. Energy supply is mainly the job of carbohydrates and fats.
Explicación (ES): Las proteínas son el material de construcción del cuerpo: forman y reparan músculos, tendones, ligamentos, enzimas y hormonas. El aporte de energía es sobre todo función de los carbohidratos y las grasas.

Question: What can happen to an athlete if he loses 3% of his body fluids during a sports performance due to perspiration?
Explanation (EN): From about 2% fluid loss, performance (endurance and strength) measurably drops. Loss of consciousness and serious heat problems occur with much larger losses.
Explicación (ES): A partir de una pérdida de líquido de aproximadamente el 2%, el rendimiento (resistencia y fuerza) baja de forma medible. La pérdida de consciencia y los problemas graves por calor ocurren con pérdidas mucho mayores.

Question: How many kcal does 1 gram of carbohydrate provide?
Explanation (EN): Carbohydrate 4 kcal/g, protein 4 kcal/g, alcohol 7 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g.
Explicación (ES): Carbohidrato 4 kcal/g, proteína 4 kcal/g, alcohol 7 kcal/g, grasa 9 kcal/g.

Question: How many kcal does 1 gram of protein provide?
Explanation (EN): Protein provides about 4 kcal per gram, the same as carbohydrate.
Explicación (ES): La proteína aporta unas 4 kcal por gramo, igual que los carbohidratos.

Question: How many kcal does 1 gram of alcohol provide?
Explanation (EN): Alcohol provides about 7 kcal per gram but no useful nutrients ('empty calories').
Explicación (ES): El alcohol aporta unas 7 kcal por gramo pero ningún nutriente útil ('calorías vacías').

Question: Which three nutrients are the macronutrients that provide energy?
Explanation (EN): The energy-providing macronutrients are carbohydrates, fats and proteins. Vitamins and minerals are micronutrients and provide no energy.
Explicación (ES): Los macronutrientes que aportan energía son los carbohidratos, las grasas y las proteínas. Las vitaminas y los minerales son micronutrientes y no aportan energía.

Question: Which nutrient is the body's preferred fuel during high-intensity exercise?
Explanation (EN): At high intensity carbohydrates (glycogen, glucose) are the main fuel because they can be broken down quickly, also anaerobically.
Explicación (ES): A alta intensidad los carbohidratos (glucógeno, glucosa) son el combustible principal porque se descomponen rápido, incluso de forma anaeróbica.

Question: What is the recommended daily protein intake for a sedentary healthy adult?
C: About 0.8 g per kg body weight
Explanation (EN): The general recommendation is about 0.8 g/kg/day. Strength athletes often benefit from about 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day.
Explicación (ES): La recomendación general es de unos 0,8 g/kg/día. Los deportistas de fuerza suelen beneficiarse de unos 1,6–2,2 g/kg/día.

Question: What protein intake is commonly advised for strength athletes who want to build muscle?
Explanation (EN): Research (e.g. ISSN position stand) supports about 1.4–2.0 g/kg/day, with benefit plateauing around 1.6–2.2 g/kg.
Explicación (ES): La investigación (p. ej., la posición de la ISSN) respalda unos 1,4–2,0 g/kg/día, y el beneficio se estabiliza alrededor de 1,6–2,2 g/kg.

Question: What are amino acids?
Explanation (EN): Proteins are chains of amino acids. Essential amino acids must come from food because the body cannot make them.
Explicación (ES): Las proteínas son cadenas de aminoácidos. Los aminoácidos esenciales deben venir de los alimentos porque el cuerpo no puede fabricarlos.

Question: How many essential amino acids are there?
Explanation (EN): There are 20 amino acids in protein; 9 are essential (must come from the diet).
Explicación (ES): Hay 20 aminoácidos en las proteínas; 9 son esenciales (deben venir de la dieta).

Question: Which fats are considered the healthiest?
Explanation (EN): Unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, oily fish) support heart health. Trans fats are the most harmful; saturated fats should be limited.
Explicación (ES): Las grasas insaturadas (aceite de oliva, frutos secos, pescado azul) favorecen la salud cardiovascular. Las grasas trans son las más perjudiciales; las saturadas deben limitarse.

Question: Omega-3 fatty acids are found mainly in...
D: Oily fish such as salmon and mackerel
Explanation (EN): Oily fish, walnuts and flaxseed are rich in omega-3, a polyunsaturated fat.
Explicación (ES): El pescado azul, las nueces y la linaza son ricos en omega-3, una grasa poliinsaturada.

Question: Which vitamins are fat-soluble?
Explanation (EN): Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and can be stored in the body. B vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble.
Explicación (ES): Las vitaminas A, D, E y K son liposolubles y se pueden almacenar en el cuerpo. Las vitaminas B y la vitamina C son hidrosolubles.

Question: Which mineral is most important for strong bones?
Explanation (EN): Calcium (together with vitamin D for absorption) is essential for bone strength.
Explicación (ES): El calcio (junto con la vitamina D para su absorción) es esencial para la fortaleza de los huesos.

Question: Which mineral is needed for oxygen transport in the blood?
Explanation (EN): Iron is part of haemoglobin, which carries oxygen. Iron deficiency causes fatigue and lower endurance.
Explicación (ES): El hierro forma parte de la hemoglobina, que transporta el oxígeno. La falta de hierro causa cansancio y menor resistencia.

Question: Which vitamin is made in the skin under the influence of sunlight?
Explanation (EN): Vitamin D is produced in the skin under UV light and helps absorb calcium.
Explicación (ES): La vitamina D se produce en la piel con la luz UV y ayuda a absorber el calcio.

Question: What is the main function of dietary fibre?
B: Supporting digestion and bowel function and giving a feeling of fullness
Explanation (EN): Fibre supports bowel function, feeds gut bacteria, slows sugar uptake and helps you feel full. Adults are advised about 30–40 g per day.
Explicación (ES): La fibra favorece el tránsito intestinal, alimenta la flora, ralentiza la absorción de azúcar y aumenta la saciedad. Se recomiendan unos 30–40 g al día para adultos.

Question: What does BMR (basal metabolic rate) mean?
B: The energy the body needs at complete rest for basic functions
D: The maximum energy you can burn
Explanation (EN): BMR is the energy needed at complete rest to keep basic functions going (breathing, circulation, temperature). It is the largest part of daily energy use.
Explicación (ES): El metabolismo basal es la energía necesaria en reposo total para mantener las funciones básicas (respiración, circulación, temperatura). Es la mayor parte del gasto diario.

Question: A client wants to lose weight. What is the basic principle?
A: Energy intake lower than energy expenditure
B: Energy intake higher than energy expenditure
D: Energy intake equal to energy expenditure
Explanation (EN): Weight loss requires a negative energy balance: you take in less energy than you use.
Explicación (ES): Perder peso requiere un balance energético negativo: ingerir menos energía de la que se gasta.

Question: How many kcal is roughly equal to 1 kg of body fat?
Explanation (EN): 1 kg of body fat stores about 7,000–7,700 kcal. (1 lb ≈ 3,500 kcal, a common trap.)
Explicación (ES): 1 kg de grasa corporal almacena unas 7.000–7.700 kcal. (1 libra ≈ 3.500 kcal, una trampa habitual.)

Question: What does the glycaemic index (GI) indicate?
A: The amount of fat in a food
B: The protein quality of a food
C: The number of calories in a food
D: How quickly a carbohydrate food raises blood sugar
Explanation (EN): High-GI foods (white bread) raise blood sugar quickly; low-GI foods (lentils, oats) raise it slowly.
Explicación (ES): Los alimentos de IG alto (pan blanco) elevan el azúcar en sangre rápidamente; los de IG bajo (lentejas, avena) lo elevan lentamente.

Question: How much water should an average adult drink per day (approximately)?
Explanation (EN): Guidelines (e.g. Voedingscentrum) advise about 1.5–2 litres of fluid per day, more with exercise and heat.
Explicación (ES): Las guías (p. ej., Voedingscentrum) aconsejan unos 1,5–2 litros de líquido al día, más con ejercicio y calor.

Question: What is a good way for a client to check hydration?
A: Amount of sweat on the shirt
D: Colour of the urine (pale yellow is good)
Explanation (EN): Pale, straw-coloured urine indicates good hydration; dark urine suggests dehydration.
Explicación (ES): Una orina de color amarillo pálido indica buena hidratación; una orina oscura sugiere deshidratación.

Question: What is the main cause of muscle cramps in endurance sports, according to the traditional explanation taught in many courses?
A: Fluid and electrolyte loss (and muscle fatigue)
Explanation (EN): Cramps are linked to muscle fatigue and to fluid/electrolyte loss through sweat. Current research points mostly to neuromuscular fatigue.
Explicación (ES): Los calambres se relacionan con la fatiga muscular y con la pérdida de líquidos/electrolitos por el sudor. La investigación actual apunta sobre todo a la fatiga neuromuscular.

Question: Which electrolyte is lost most through sweat?
Explanation (EN): Sweat contains mostly sodium (salt), plus smaller amounts of potassium.
Explicación (ES): El sudor contiene sobre todo sodio (sal), además de cantidades menores de potasio.

Question: What is a good recovery meal after strength training?
A: A combination of protein and carbohydrates
Explanation (EN): Protein (about 20–40 g) supports muscle repair, carbohydrates refill glycogen.
Explicación (ES): La proteína (unos 20–40 g) favorece la reparación muscular y los carbohidratos reponen el glucógeno.

Question: Which statement about carbohydrates is correct?
A: They are only found in sugar
B: They are stored as glycogen in liver and muscles in limited amounts
C: They are stored without limit in the body
Explanation (EN): Glycogen stores are limited (roughly 400–500 g in total), which is why long efforts need carbohydrate intake.
Explicación (ES): Las reservas de glucógeno son limitadas (unos 400–500 g en total), por eso los esfuerzos largos requieren ingerir carbohidratos.

Question: What is the 'Schijf van Vijf' / healthy plate model mainly used for?
D: Giving guidance on a varied and healthy diet
Explanation (EN): The Dutch 'Schijf van Vijf' (Wheel of Five) from the Voedingscentrum shows which food groups to eat for a healthy, varied diet.
Explicación (ES): La 'Schijf van Vijf' (Rueda de Cinco) del Voedingscentrum neerlandés muestra qué grupos de alimentos comer para una dieta sana y variada.

Question: What is the main function of carbohydrates?
Explanation (EN): Carbohydrates are mainly an energy source, especially for the brain and for intense exercise.
Explicación (ES): Los carbohidratos son principalmente una fuente de energía, sobre todo para el cerebro y el ejercicio intenso.

Question: Which is a complete protein source (contains all essential amino acids)?
Explanation (EN): Animal proteins (eggs, meat, fish, dairy) and soy contain all essential amino acids. Plant sources can be combined to cover them.
Explicación (ES): Las proteínas animales (huevos, carne, pescado, lácteos) y la soja contienen todos los aminoácidos esenciales. Las fuentes vegetales pueden combinarse para cubrirlos.

Question: A supplement that has good scientific evidence for improving short, high-intensity performance is...
Explanation (EN): Creatine monohydrate is one of the best-researched supplements: it increases creatine phosphate stores and improves repeated high-intensity efforts.
Explicación (ES): La creatina monohidrato es uno de los suplementos más estudiados: aumenta las reservas de fosfocreatina y mejora los esfuerzos repetidos de alta intensidad.

Question: Which nutrient has the largest effect on satiety (feeling full) per kcal?
Explanation (EN): Protein is the most satiating macronutrient and also costs more energy to digest (thermic effect).
Explicación (ES): La proteína es el macronutriente más saciante y además requiere más energía para digerirse (efecto térmico).

Question: What does the 'C' of the ICE rule mean?
Explanation (EN): ICE = Ice (cooling), Compression, Elevation. Compression limits swelling after an acute injury such as a sprained ankle.
Explicación (ES): ICE = Ice (hielo/enfriar), Compression (compresión), Elevation (elevación). La compresión limita la hinchazón tras una lesión aguda como un esguince de tobillo.

Question: While running on the treadmill, a person's ankle breaks. He can no longer stand on it. How long do you have to cool?
Explanation (EN): Following the ICE rule, cool the injured area for about 20 minutes (with a cloth between ice and skin) and call professional help for a suspected fracture. Do not move the ankle.
Explicación (ES): Siguiendo la regla ICE, enfría la zona lesionada unos 20 minutos (con un paño entre el hielo y la piel) y pide ayuda profesional ante una posible fractura. No muevas el tobillo.
Note: Answer not confirmed by the portal. Check this one in your course book.

Question: What does the 'E' of the ICE rule stand for?
Explanation (EN): Elevation: raise the injured limb above heart level to reduce swelling.
Explicación (ES): Elevation (elevación): eleva el miembro lesionado por encima del nivel del corazón para reducir la hinchazón.

Question: Why should you never put ice directly on the skin?
Explanation (EN): Direct contact can freeze the skin. Always use a cloth or towel between ice and skin.
Explicación (ES): El contacto directo puede congelar la piel. Usa siempre un paño o toalla entre el hielo y la piel.

Question: What is the difference between a sprain and a strain?
A: A strain is always more serious
B: A sprain is a muscle injury; a strain is a bone injury
D: A sprain is a ligament injury; a strain is a muscle or tendon injury
Explanation (EN): Sprain = ligament (e.g. ankle sprain). Strain = muscle or tendon (e.g. pulled hamstring). Tip: strain has a 't' for tendon.
Explicación (ES): Esguince (sprain) = ligamento (p. ej., esguince de tobillo). Distensión (strain) = músculo o tendón (p. ej., rotura de isquiotibial). Truco: strain tiene una 't' de tendon.

Question: An inflammation of a tendon is called...
Explanation (EN): Tendinitis/tendinopathy is irritation of a tendon, usually due to overload. Bursitis is inflammation of a bursa.
Explicación (ES): La tendinitis/tendinopatía es la irritación de un tendón, normalmente por sobrecarga. La bursitis es la inflamación de una bolsa sinovial.

Question: What is the first thing you do when someone collapses in the gym and does not respond?
C: Wait to see if they wake up
D: Check for danger, then check responsiveness and breathing, and call for help (112)
Explanation (EN): Make sure the area is safe, check responsiveness and breathing, call 112 (or have someone call) and get the AED if they are not breathing normally.
Explicación (ES): Asegúrate de que la zona es segura, comprueba si responde y respira, llama al 112 (o pide que alguien llame) y trae el DEA si no respira con normalidad.

Question: What is the emergency number in the Netherlands and most of Europe?
Explanation (EN): 112 is the European emergency number.
Explicación (ES): El 112 es el número de emergencias europeo.

Question: What does AED stand for?
Explanation (EN): AED = Automated External Defibrillator. It analyses heart rhythm and gives a shock if needed.
Explicación (ES): DEA = Desfibrilador Externo Automático. Analiza el ritmo cardíaco y da una descarga si es necesario.

Question: What is the ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths in adult CPR?
Explanation (EN): Adult CPR: 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths, at 100–120 compressions per minute.
Explicación (ES): RCP en adultos: 30 compresiones torácicas seguidas de 2 insuflaciones, a 100–120 compresiones por minuto.

Question: A diabetic client feels shaky, sweaty and confused during training. What is most likely happening?
Explanation (EN): These are signs of hypoglycaemia. Stop the exercise and give fast-acting sugar (e.g. glucose tablets, lemonade).
Explicación (ES): Son signos de hipoglucemia. Detén el ejercicio y da azúcar de acción rápida (p. ej., tabletas de glucosa, refresco azucarado).

Question: Which symptom during exercise is a reason to stop immediately?
C: Muscle fatigue at the end of a set
Explanation (EN): Chest pain, severe breathlessness, dizziness, fainting or irregular heartbeat are warning signs: stop and seek medical help.
Explicación (ES): El dolor u opresión en el pecho, la falta de aire intensa, los mareos, el desmayo o el latido irregular son señales de alarma: detén el ejercicio y busca ayuda médica.

Question: A client faints in the gym but is breathing normally. What position do you put them in?
Explanation (EN): An unresponsive person who is breathing normally goes in the recovery position to keep the airway open. Call 112 and keep checking breathing.
Explicación (ES): Una persona inconsciente que respira con normalidad se coloca en posición lateral de seguridad para mantener la vía aérea abierta. Llama al 112 y sigue comprobando la respiración.

Question: What is the main purpose of the ICE rule after an acute injury?
Explanation (EN): Cooling, compression and elevation limit swelling, internal bleeding and pain in the first phase after an acute injury.
Explicación (ES): Enfriar, comprimir y elevar limitan la hinchazón, la hemorragia interna y el dolor en la primera fase tras una lesión aguda.

Question: What is an acute injury?
A: An injury of the skin only
C: An injury that develops slowly through repeated overload
D: An injury that happens suddenly due to a single event
Explanation (EN): Acute injury: sudden, clear moment (sprain, fracture). Overuse injury: gradual, from repeated overload (tendinopathy, shin splints).
Explicación (ES): Lesión aguda: repentina, con un momento claro (esguince, fractura). Lesión por sobrecarga: gradual, por sobrecarga repetida (tendinopatía, periostitis tibial).

Question: Which is an example of an overuse injury?
Explanation (EN): Shin splints (medial tibial stress syndrome) develop gradually through repeated overload, typically in runners.
Explicación (ES): La periostitis tibial (síndrome de estrés tibial medial) se desarrolla gradualmente por sobrecarga repetida, típicamente en corredores.

Question: How can a fitness trainer best prevent overuse injuries in clients?
A: Train the same exercise every day
C: Build up load gradually and plan enough recovery
Explanation (EN): Gradual progression with adequate recovery keeps load within load capacity, which prevents overload.
Explicación (ES): Una progresión gradual con recuperación suficiente mantiene la carga dentro de la capacidad de carga, lo que previene la sobrecarga.

Question: What is the safest action when you notice a broken or faulty machine in the gym?
A: Put it out of use (mark it) and report it immediately
B: Tell clients to avoid it only if they ask
C: Fix it yourself during a session
Explanation (EN): Mark the equipment as out of order, prevent use and report it so it can be repaired. This is part of your duty of care.
Explicación (ES): Marca el equipo como fuera de servicio, impide su uso e infórmalo para que se repare. Forma parte de tu deber de cuidado.

Question: What is the best way to prevent clients from being injured by free weights lying on the floor?
A: Leave them; clients will see them
D: Keep the training area tidy and put weights back in the rack
Explanation (EN): A tidy training floor prevents tripping and falling. Encourage clients to rack weights after use.
Explicación (ES): Una zona de entrenamiento ordenada evita tropiezos y caídas. Anima a los clientes a devolver los pesos a su sitio.

Question: A client has high blood pressure (hypertension). What should you avoid?
C: Holding the breath and very heavy isometric efforts (Valsalva)
Explanation (EN): Breath-holding and very heavy straining raise blood pressure sharply. Moderate aerobic and dynamic strength training with proper breathing are recommended.
Explicación (ES): Contener la respiración y los esfuerzos muy pesados elevan bruscamente la presión arterial. Se recomienda entrenamiento aeróbico moderado y de fuerza dinámica con buena respiración.

Question: What is a contra-indication?
D: A reason why a certain exercise or training should not be done
Explanation (EN): A contra-indication is a condition or factor that makes a treatment or exercise inadvisable (e.g. exercise with a fever).
Explicación (ES): Una contraindicación es una condición o factor que hace desaconsejable un tratamiento o ejercicio (p. ej., hacer ejercicio con fiebre).

Question: A client has a fever. What do you advise?
B: Train hard to sweat it out
C: Do not train until the fever has gone
Explanation (EN): Exercising with a fever is a contra-indication: it increases the risk of heart muscle inflammation (myocarditis). Rest until recovered.
Explicación (ES): Hacer ejercicio con fiebre está contraindicado: aumenta el riesgo de inflamación del músculo cardíaco (miocarditis). Descansar hasta recuperarse.

Question: What are the classic signs of inflammation?
C: Redness, heat, swelling, pain and loss of function
Explanation (EN): The five classic signs: rubor (redness), calor (heat), tumor (swelling), dolor (pain) and functio laesa (loss of function).
Explicación (ES): Los cinco signos clásicos: rubor (enrojecimiento), calor, tumor (hinchazón), dolor y functio laesa (pérdida de función).

Question: What is heat stroke?
C: A muscle cramp due to heat
D: A life-threatening rise in body temperature where the body can no longer cool itself
Explanation (EN): Heat stroke: core temperature above about 40 °C with confusion. Call 112 and cool the person down immediately.
Explicación (ES): Golpe de calor: temperatura central por encima de unos 40 °C con confusión. Llama al 112 y enfría a la persona inmediatamente.

Question: Who is responsible for creating a safe training environment during a personal training session?
Explanation (EN): The trainer has a duty of care: check equipment, space, technique and the client's health status.
Explicación (ES): El entrenador tiene un deber de cuidado: revisar el equipo, el espacio, la técnica y el estado de salud del cliente.

Question: A client with lower back pain asks for advice. What is the right action for a fitness trainer?
A: Diagnose the cause and treat it
B: Refer to a (sports) physiotherapist or doctor if pain is unexplained, severe or persistent
D: Tell them to rest for 6 weeks
Explanation (EN): A fitness trainer does not diagnose. Refer to a medical professional when needed and stay within your scope of practice.
Explicación (ES): Un entrenador de fitness no diagnostica. Deriva a un profesional sanitario cuando sea necesario y mantente dentro de tus competencias.

Question: What is a common sign of dehydration?
A: Dark urine, thirst, headache and fatigue
Explanation (EN): Dark urine, thirst, headache, dizziness and fatigue indicate dehydration.
Explicación (ES): La orina oscura, la sed, el dolor de cabeza, los mareos y la fatiga indican deshidratación.

Question: What is the main risk of a cool-down that is skipped after very intensive exercise?
A: Blood pooling in the legs, which can cause dizziness or fainting
Explanation (EN): Stopping suddenly removes the muscle pump; blood can pool in the legs and blood pressure drops, causing dizziness.
